title: AZ-104 distinctions
_note: Cards are distinctions, not definitions. Each front is a question the exam asks by implication; each back is the shortest true answer. 'module' points at the lesson that teaches it and cites the source. Scheduling is Leitner: 1, 3, 7, 16, 35 days.

cards.front: Security group vs Microsoft 365 group: which can contain devices?
cards.back: Security groups only. Microsoft 365 group members can only be users.

cards.front: Can you add a member to a dynamic group by hand?
cards.back: No. Change the rule, or the attribute the rule reads.

cards.front: Dynamic group licensing: assigned or counted?
cards.back: Counted. Each unique user member needs an Entra ID P1 licence in the organisation, but you don't assign it to them. Devices need none.

cards.front: Licence assignment fails for a new user. First thing to check?
cards.back: Usage location. A licence can't be assigned without it; group-based licensing falls back to the tenant location.

cards.front: Group-based licensing and nested groups?
cards.back: Not supported. Only first-level members of the licensed group get the licence.

cards.front: External collaboration settings vs cross-tenant access settings: which wins?
cards.back: Neither. The most restrictive setting applies.

cards.front: Least-privileged role to let one user invite guests?
cards.back: Guest Inviter. It works even when invitations are limited to admin roles.

cards.front: SSPR 'Selected': how many groups in the admin center?
cards.back: One. Nested groups inside it are supported.

cards.front: Why test SSPR with a non-admin account?
cards.back: Admin role holders follow a fixed two-gate policy (two methods, no security questions) that ignores your user policy.

cards.front: How long can a deleted Entra user be restored?
cards.back: 30 days. Its licences come back too, even if that over-consumes.

cards.front: What are the three parts of an Azure role assignment?
cards.back: Security principal (who), role definition (what), scope (where).

cards.front: Contributor vs Owner: what's the one difference that matters?
cards.back: Contributor can't assign roles or policies: its NotActions exclude Microsoft.Authorization write and delete.

cards.front: User Access Administrator vs Role Based Access Control Administrator?
cards.back: Both assign roles, including Owner. RBAC Administrator can only create and delete role assignments; it can't manage access through Azure Policy.

cards.front: Is NotActions a deny?
cards.back: No. It trims one role's wildcard. Another role granting the action still grants it. Only deny assignments deny.

cards.front: Can you create a deny assignment yourself?
cards.back: No. Azure creates them, for example for a deployment stack with deny settings.

cards.front: Does Owner let you read blob data with your Entra identity?
cards.back: No. Owner, Contributor and Reader have no DataActions. Use a data role such as Storage Blob Data Reader.

cards.front: Global Administrator can't see subscriptions. Fix?
cards.back: Elevate access (Access management for Azure resources): User Access Administrator at root scope /. Turn it off afterwards.

cards.front: az role assignment list shows nothing, but the user has access. Why?
cards.back: Default is direct assignments at the current subscription only. Add --all, --include-inherited, --include-groups.

cards.front: Check access at a subscription: does it show a resource-group assignment?
cards.back: No. It shows the scope and what's inherited to it, never child scopes.

cards.front: Role assignment limits?
cards.back: 5,000 per subscription (fixed; management groups not counted), 500 per management group. Assign to groups.

cards.front: Does a deny policy fix or delete existing non-compliant resources?
cards.back: No. It marks them non-compliant and blocks new or updated ones. Fix existing ones with modify or deployIfNotExists plus a remediation task.

cards.front: What runs a remediation task, and with what permissions?
cards.back: The policy assignment's managed identity, with the roles the definition needs. The portal grants them; an SDK doesn't.

cards.front: Exclusion vs exemption?
cards.back: Exclusion (notScopes): not evaluated, not counted. Exemption (Waiver or Mitigated): shown as Exempted, can expire.

cards.front: How long before new policy compliance shows?
cards.back: About 5 minutes for a new assignment to apply, about 15 for a changed resource, and a full scan every 24 hours. Or trigger a scan.

cards.front: CanNotDelete vs ReadOnly lock?
cards.back: CanNotDelete: read and modify, no delete. ReadOnly: read only, and it blocks POSTs (VM restart, list storage keys).

cards.front: Who can create locks? Does a lock stop an Owner?
cards.back: Owner or User Access Administrator (Microsoft.Authorization/locks/*), not Contributor. Yes: locks apply to everyone.

cards.front: Can you lock or tag a management group?
cards.back: Neither. Locks and tags go on subscriptions, resource groups and resources.

cards.front: Do resources inherit resource group tags?
cards.back: No. Use an Inherit a tag policy (modify) plus remediation for existing resources.

cards.front: Tag limits?
cards.back: 50 per resource, resource group or subscription. Name 512 characters (128 for storage accounts), value 256. Names case-insensitive, values case-sensitive.

cards.front: What changes when you move a resource to another resource group?
cards.back: Its resource ID changes; its region doesn't. Both resource groups are locked for up to 4 hours; the resource keeps running.

cards.front: Move resources to a subscription in another tenant?
cards.back: Not supported. Change the subscription's directory, or re-create the resources.

cards.front: What does Change directory on a subscription delete?
cards.back: All Azure role assignments and custom roles, permanently, plus Azure Policy objects. Managed identities must be re-enabled or re-created.

cards.front: Where do new subscriptions land? How deep can management groups go?
cards.back: Under the root management group, unless a default management group is set. Six levels, not counting root or subscriptions; 10,000 groups.

cards.front: Budget alert fired but VMs still run. Why?
cards.back: Budgets notify; they don't cap. Attach an action group that runs automation.

cards.front: Advisor ignores month-end peaks. Fix?
cards.back: Change the right-sizing lookback period from the default 7 days to 14, 21, 30, 60 or 90.

cards.front: The two gates for every storage data request?
cards.back: Network (the storage firewall) and authorization (Entra role, Shared Key, SAS, or Files identity). Both must pass.

cards.front: Can an IP rule use 10.1.1.0/24? A /32?
cards.back: No private (RFC 1918) ranges. No /31 or /32 prefixes: enter the single IP. IPv4 only.

cards.front: Why can't IP rules restrict a same-region VM?
cards.back: Same-region traffic uses private Azure addresses. Use a virtual network rule with a Microsoft.Storage service endpoint.

cards.front: Firewall on, settings editable, but the portal can't list blobs. Why?
cards.back: The firewall covers the data plane only. Browsing blobs is data plane: add your client IP.

cards.front: User delegation SAS: signed with, max validity, affected by key rotation?
cards.back: A user delegation key from Entra credentials; 7 days; not affected by key rotation.

cards.front: Which SAS can use a stored access policy?
cards.back: Only a service SAS. Up to five policies per container.

cards.front: How do you revoke a leaked ad hoc account SAS immediately?
cards.back: Regenerate the account key that signed it. That's the only immediate way.

cards.front: Deleted a stored access policy, then re-created it with the same name. Effect?
cards.back: The old tokens that reference it become valid again, if they haven't expired. Use a new name.

cards.front: Key expiration policy: does it rotate keys?
cards.back: No. It's a rotation reminder, which Azure Policy can report on.

cards.front: What does AllowSharedKeyAccess = false break and keep?
cards.back: Breaks account keys and every service or account SAS (403). Keeps Entra auth and user delegation SAS. Required for Conditional Access.

cards.front: Azure Files identity sources, and how many per account?
cards.back: AD DS, Microsoft Entra Domain Services, Microsoft Entra Kerberos. One per storage account, for all its shares.

cards.front: Which Files identity source needs no DC line of sight?
cards.back: Microsoft Entra Kerberos (Entra-joined or hybrid-joined clients).

cards.front: Default share-level permission: starting value, and when to use it?
cards.back: None. Use it when identities aren't synced to Entra (or for computer accounts). It applies to all authenticated identities.

cards.front: Share role granted but root folder access denied?
cards.back: Windows ACLs on the root still decide. A share-level role only admits the user to the share.

cards.front: Can a storage account's type change after creation?
cards.back: No. Create a new account and copy the data.

cards.front: Storage account name rules?
cards.back: 3-24 characters, lowercase letters and numbers only, unique across Azure.

cards.front: Which redundancy options do Premium accounts support?
cards.back: LRS and ZRS only. No geo-redundancy.

cards.front: GRS vs RA-GRS?
cards.back: Both copy asynchronously to the paired region. Only RA-GRS lets you read the secondary without failover.

cards.front: Can you choose the secondary region?
cards.back: No. It's the paired region, set by the primary.

cards.front: ZRS to GRS?
cards.back: No direct path: two steps via GZRS or LRS, at least 24 hours apart.

cards.front: Zonal conversion timing?
cards.back: Usually starts within about 72 hours, can take weeks, no completion SLA, no downtime.

cards.front: Removing RA from RA-GRS: billing?
cards.back: Still billed as RA for 30 days after the change.

cards.front: Object replication prerequisites?
cards.back: Blob versioning on both accounts; change feed on the source. Block blobs only; no hierarchical namespace.

cards.front: Object replication: destination container behaviour?
cards.back: Read-only while a rule targets it: writes fail with 409. Existing blobs aren't copied by default.

cards.front: Customer-managed key requirements?
cards.back: Key Vault or Managed HSM with soft delete and purge protection; RSA key of 2048, 3072 or 4096 bits; managed identity with get, wrapkey and unwrapkey.

cards.front: When can infrastructure encryption be enabled?
cards.back: Only when creating the account or encryption scope.

cards.front: Encryption scopes: purpose and deletion?
cards.back: A separate key per container or blob. Can't be deleted, only disabled.

cards.front: AzCopy between two accounts: through your PC?
cards.back: No. azcopy copy uses server-to-server APIs.

cards.front: azcopy sync direction and scope?
cards.back: One-way; between local storage and Blob Storage, or between containers.

cards.front: Owner of the account, AzCopy with Entra returns 403?
cards.back: Owner has no data role. Assign Storage Blob Data Contributor, or use a SAS.

cards.front: Azure Files billing model recommended for new shares?
cards.back: Provisioned v2: storage, IOPS and throughput provisioned separately.

cards.front: Pay-as-you-go file share tiers?
cards.back: Transaction optimized, hot, cool (HDD). Up to 5 tier changes in 30 days, not twice within 24 hours.

cards.front: NFS file share requirements?
cards.back: SSD with a provisioned billing model.

cards.front: Container access levels?
cards.back: Private (none), Blob (read blobs), Container (read blobs and list the container). The account must allow anonymous access.

cards.front: Minimum stays for cool, cold, archive?
cards.back: 30, 90 and 180 days. Leaving early costs a prorated early-deletion charge.

cards.front: Which redundancy options support archive?
cards.back: LRS, GRS and RA-GRS only. Not ZRS, GZRS or RA-GZRS.

cards.front: Rehydration priorities?
cards.back: Standard (default, up to 15 hours) or High (under 1 hour for blobs under 10 GB). Can raise, not lower.

cards.front: Rehydrate without an early-deletion fee?
cards.back: Copy Blob to a new blob name in an online tier.

cards.front: Can lifecycle management rehydrate?
cards.back: No. It only tiers cooler or deletes. It runs once a day.

cards.front: Stop a lifecycle rule re-archiving rehydrated blobs?
cards.back: Add daysAfterLastTierChangeGreaterThan to tierToArchive, or rehydrate by copying.

cards.front: Rule by last READ time needs what?
cards.back: Access time tracking enabled, plus daysAfterLastAccessTimeGreaterThan.

cards.front: Blob soft delete vs container soft delete?
cards.back: Separate settings, 1-365 days each. Blob soft delete never restores a container.

cards.front: Restore a soft-deleted container: any name?
cards.back: Original name only, and not if a new container with that name exists.

cards.front: Versioning on, blob deleted, Undelete clicked: restored?
cards.back: No. Promote a previous version (Make current version).

cards.front: Control versioning costs?
cards.back: A lifecycle rule deleting previous versions by age.

cards.front: Share snapshots: limits and properties?
cards.back: Up to 200 per share; read-only, incremental, whole share; restore individual files.

cards.front: Share soft delete default and scope?
cards.back: On by default for new accounts, 7 days (1-365). Restores whole shares only.

cards.front: Which ARM template section is required besides $schema and contentVersion?
cards.back: resources. parameters, variables, functions and outputs are optional.

cards.front: What does Bicep become before deployment?
cards.back: An ARM JSON template. Resource Manager only deploys JSON; the CLI and PowerShell build Bicep for you.

cards.front: Resources without dependsOn: deployment order?
cards.back: In parallel. dependsOn forces ordering; list only resources in the same template.

cards.front: Bicep: when is dependsOn generated automatically?
cards.back: When a resource references another by symbolic name, including parent:.

cards.front: uniqueString(resourceGroup().id): random?
cards.back: No. Deterministic: same input, same value. Unique per resource group, repeatable.

cards.front: Keep a password out of deployment history?
cards.back: securestring or secureobject in ARM; @secure() in Bicep.

cards.front: Restrict parameter values?
cards.back: allowedValues in ARM; @allowed([...]) in Bicep.

cards.front: Reference a resource without deploying it (Bicep)?
cards.back: Declare it with the existing keyword.

cards.front: Incremental vs complete mode?
cards.back: Incremental (default) leaves extra resources alone. Complete deletes resources in the group not in the template.

cards.front: Preview a deployment's changes?
cards.back: what-if: az deployment group what-if, or New-AzResourceGroupDeployment -WhatIf. --confirm-with-what-if previews then asks.

cards.front: Deploy at subscription scope (CLI and PowerShell)?
cards.back: az deployment sub create; New-AzSubscriptionDeployment.

cards.front: Export as Bicep: where?
cards.back: Only in the portal. The CLI and PowerShell export ARM JSON; decompile it to get Bicep.

cards.front: The exact template a past deployment used?
cards.back: Resource group > Deployments > the deployment > Template (ARM JSON).

cards.front: Is bicep decompile exact?
cards.back: Best-effort. Output is functionally equivalent but may need cleanup; round trips aren't identical.

cards.front: Export template limits?
cards.back: Not guaranteed; may omit passwords and use older API versions; fails above 200 resources.

cards.front: Stopped vs deallocated VM billing?
cards.back: Stopped from inside the OS: compute still billed. Deallocated: compute not billed. Disks bill either way.

cards.front: Is the temporary disk persistent?
cards.back: No. It isn't a managed disk; data can be lost on deallocation, redeploy or maintenance.

cards.front: Resize to a size not in the list?
cards.back: Deallocate first. Resizing restarts the VM; deallocating releases dynamic IPs.

cards.front: Which disk types can't be OS disks?
cards.back: Ultra Disk and Premium SSD v2. Standard HDD OS disks retire September 8, 2028.

cards.front: Grow a data disk online?
cards.back: Yes. Exception: a disk of 4 TiB or less (HDD, Standard SSD, Premium SSD) going beyond 4 TiB needs deallocate and detach.

cards.front: Shrink a managed disk?
cards.back: Not possible. Create a smaller disk and copy the data.

cards.front: Change disk type (e.g. to Premium SSD)?
cards.back: Stop the VM; Premium needs a size that supports Premium storage. The conversion is instant.

cards.front: What does encryption at host add to SSE?
cards.back: Encryption of the temporary disk and caches, with data flowing encrypted to storage; no VM CPU used.

cards.front: Encryption at host prerequisites?
cards.back: Register the EncryptionAtHost feature on the subscription; deallocate an existing VM before changing it.

cards.front: Azure Disk Encryption retirement?
cards.back: September 15, 2028. Use encryption at host for new VMs.

cards.front: Move a VM to another region?
cards.back: Azure Resource Mover. Resource group and subscription moves use the standard move.

cards.front: Move a VM to another VNet?
cards.back: Not supported. Re-create the VM from its disk in the target VNet.

cards.front: Availability set limits and timing?
cards.back: Up to 3 fault domains and 20 update domains; 99.95%; VMs join only at creation.

cards.front: Availability zones SLA?
cards.back: 99.99% for VMs across two or more zones.

cards.front: Scale set orchestration: recommended and changeable?
cards.back: Flexible is recommended; the mode is fixed at creation.

cards.front: Flexible scale set outbound internet?
cards.back: No default outbound access. Configure NAT gateway, load balancer outbound rules or public IPs.

cards.front: Autoscale scale-in logic?
cards.back: Scales in only if ALL scale-in rules trigger. Any scale-out rule triggers scale-out, to the highest capacity asked.

cards.front: Which ACR tier has geo-replication and private endpoints?
cards.back: Premium.

cards.front: Least-privilege role to pull from ACR? To push?
cards.back: AcrPull to pull; AcrPush to push and pull. Both are data-plane only.

cards.front: Copy an image into ACR without Docker?
cards.back: az acr import.

cards.front: What does an ACI container group share?
cards.back: Host, lifecycle, local network (localhost), IP and DNS label, and volumes. Multi-container is Linux only.

cards.front: ACI restart policies and default?
cards.back: Always (default), OnFailure, Never. Never prevents restart after a successful exit.

cards.front: Persist data from ACI?
cards.back: Mount an Azure Files share (Linux containers).

cards.front: ACI properties that need delete and re-create?
cards.back: OS type, CPU, memory or GPU, restart policy, network profile, availability zone.

cards.front: ACI pull from ACR with managed identity: which kind?
cards.back: User-assigned only, set with --assign-identity and --acr-identity, with AcrPull.

cards.front: Does ACI autoscale?
cards.back: No rule-based scaling. Size the group; run more groups for more capacity.

cards.front: Container Apps replica defaults?
cards.back: Minimum 0 (scale to zero), maximum 10; configurable up to 1,000.

cards.front: Container Apps rules that can't scale to zero?
cards.back: CPU and memory rules. HTTP, TCP and event rules can.

cards.front: Container Apps revision modes?
cards.back: Single (default; new revision replaces the old with no downtime) and multiple (traffic splitting, weights total 100).

cards.front: Container Apps pull from ACR with system identity?
cards.back: Yes: az containerapp registry set --identity system; the identity needs AcrPull.

cards.front: Do apps in one App Service plan share compute?
cards.back: Yes. Every app runs on all the plan's instances. Isolate an app by giving it its own plan.

cards.front: How are dedicated App Service tiers billed?
cards.back: Per instance, whether apps are busy or not. Features like slots and backups cost nothing extra.

cards.front: Scale up vs scale out?
cards.back: Up: change the tier (bigger instances, more features). Out: more instances (Basic 3, Standard 10, Premium 30, Isolated 100).

cards.front: Rule-based autoscale vs automatic scaling?
cards.back: Autoscale: Standard and higher, metric rules. Automatic scaling: Premium v2 and higher, HTTP-driven, maximum burst up to 30.

cards.front: Lowest tier for a TLS binding?
cards.back: Basic (SNI). IP-based SSL needs Standard and bills hourly. Free and Shared have none.

cards.front: Free managed certificate limits?
cards.back: No wildcard, not exportable, not in App Service Environments; renews automatically.

cards.front: DNS records for www.contoso.com?
cards.back: CNAME www -> <app>.azurewebsites.net, plus TXT asuid.www with the verification ID.

cards.front: DNS records for the root contoso.com?
cards.back: A record @ -> the app's IP, plus TXT asuid with the verification ID.

cards.front: Automatic vs custom App Service backups?
cards.back: Automatic: hourly, 30 days, no setup, not downloadable. Custom: storage account, at most every 2 hours, 10 GB, downloadable.

cards.front: What isn't restored from an App Service backup?
cards.back: Custom domains, TLS bindings, managed identities, network features, scale-out settings, slots.

cards.front: Access restrictions: default behaviour?
cards.back: No rules: allow all. One rule: implicit deny for unmatched traffic. The main and scm sites have separate rules.

cards.front: Does a private endpoint respect access restrictions?
cards.back: No. Private endpoint traffic bypasses them; filter it with an NSG.

cards.front: Is VNet integration inbound or outbound?
cards.back: Outbound only. Private inbound access needs a private endpoint.

cards.front: Deployment slots: tier and count?
cards.back: Standard and higher; Standard allows 5. No extra charge.

cards.front: What does a sticky (deployment slot) setting do?
cards.back: Stays with its slot during a swap. Unmarked app settings travel with the app.

cards.front: Swap with preview?
cards.back: Applies the target's slot settings to the source and pauses for validation; then complete or cancel.

cards.front: Reserved addresses per subnet?
cards.back: Five: .0 network, .1 gateway, .2 and .3 DNS, and the last (broadcast). A /24 has 251 usable.

cards.front: Smallest IPv4 subnet, and its usable addresses?
cards.back: /29, with 3 usable. IPv6 subnets must be /64.

cards.front: Default outbound access for new VNets?
cards.back: Private subnets by default (API after March 31, 2026; portal already). VMs need a NAT gateway, public IP or LB outbound rules.

cards.front: Peering states?
cards.back: Initiated (one link), Connected (both links), Disconnected (one link deleted: re-create both).

cards.front: Is peering transitive?
cards.back: No. A-B and B-C doesn't give A-C. Peer directly, or route through a hub NVA.

cards.front: Peer VNets with overlapping address spaces?
cards.back: Not possible.

cards.front: After resizing a peered VNet?
cards.back: Sync the peering on each link.

cards.front: Use remote gateways: how many peerings?
cards.back: Only one per virtual network, and that network can't have its own gateway.

cards.front: Basic public IP status?
cards.back: Retired September 30, 2025. Use Standard: static, zone-redundant, closed inbound by default.

cards.front: Is an unattached Standard public IP billed?
cards.back: Yes, while it exists.

cards.front: Route tables per subnet?
cards.back: Zero or one. Up to 400 routes per table by default.

cards.front: UDR next hop types?
cards.back: Virtual appliance (with IP), virtual network gateway, virtual network, internet, None (drop).

cards.front: How does Azure pick a route?
cards.back: Longest prefix match, then UDR > BGP > system for the same prefix.

cards.front: NVA receives traffic but drops it?
cards.back: Enable IP forwarding on its NIC (and in its OS).

cards.front: Next hop vs IP flow verify?
cards.back: Next hop: routing (where it goes). IP flow verify: NSG rules (allowed or denied, which rule).

cards.front: NSG flow logs status?
cards.back: No new ones after June 30, 2025; retire September 30, 2027. Use virtual network flow logs.

cards.front: NSG rule priority range and processing?
cards.back: 100-4096; lowest number first; processing stops at the first match.

cards.front: NSG default inbound rules?
cards.back: AllowVNetInBound 65000, AllowAzureLoadBalancerInBound 65001, DenyAllInBound 65500.

cards.front: NSG default outbound rules?
cards.back: AllowVnetOutBound 65000, AllowInternetOutBound 65001, DenyAllOutBound 65500.

cards.front: Order: subnet NSG vs NIC NSG?
cards.back: Inbound: subnet then NIC. Outbound: NIC then subnet. Both must allow.

cards.front: What is an application security group?
cards.back: A named group of NICs used as an NSG rule source or destination. Members must share a VNet.

cards.front: Which rule blocked this packet?
cards.back: Network Watcher IP flow verify.

cards.front: All rules applied to a NIC, combined?
cards.back: Effective security rules (VM must be running).

cards.front: Bastion Developer: cost and limits?
cards.back: Free; one VM at a time; no peering; select regions; no AzureBastionSubnet or public IP.

cards.front: Dedicated Bastion subnet?
cards.back: AzureBastionSubnet, /26 or larger, plus a Standard static public IP (Premium can be private-only).

cards.front: Bastion SKU for native client and file transfer?
cards.back: Standard (or Premium). Premium adds session recording.

cards.front: Can you downgrade a Bastion SKU?
cards.back: No. Upgrade in place; downgrade means delete and re-create.

cards.front: Service endpoint: what changes?
cards.back: The subnet's source IP to the service becomes private. DNS and the destination stay public. Free.

cards.front: Service endpoint from on-premises?
cards.back: Not supported. Use a private endpoint (or allow on-premises public IPs on the firewall).

cards.front: Private endpoint: what is it?
cards.back: A NIC with a private IP in your subnet, mapped to one resource; works from peered and on-premises networks; bills hourly.

cards.front: Private endpoint DNS zone for blobs?
cards.back: privatelink.blob.core.windows.net, linked to the VNet, so the normal name resolves to the private IP.

cards.front: Is Azure DNS a registrar?
cards.back: No. It's authoritative hosting. Delegate by setting the domain's NS records at the registrar to the four Azure name servers.

cards.front: CNAME at the zone apex?
cards.back: Not allowed (and a CNAME set holds one record). Use an alias record to an Azure resource.

cards.front: What does an alias record do?
cards.back: Points at an Azure resource (public IP, Traffic Manager, CDN, Front Door...), tracks IP changes, empties if the resource is deleted, works at the apex.

cards.front: Who can resolve a private DNS zone?
cards.back: Only VNets linked to it. Linked VNets resolve each other's names without peering.

cards.front: Auto-registration rules?
cards.back: Registers A records for VMs' primary NICs; one registration zone per VNet; no PTR, no load balancers.

cards.front: Private zones with a custom DNS server?
cards.back: Bypassed. Forward the zone to 168.63.129.16 or use Azure DNS Private Resolver.

cards.front: Load balancer components?
cards.back: Frontend IP, backend pool, health probe, load-balancing rule; plus inbound NAT rules and outbound rules.

cards.front: Default distribution mode?
cards.back: 5-tuple hash. Session persistence: client IP (2-tuple) or client IP and protocol (3-tuple).

cards.front: Standard load balancer security model?
cards.back: Secure by default: inbound closed unless an NSG allows it. Basic was retired September 30, 2025.

cards.front: What are HA ports?
cards.back: A rule (protocol All, port 0) balancing all ports and protocols; internal Standard load balancer only; for NVAs.

cards.front: Health probe source address?
cards.back: 168.63.129.16 (AzureLoadBalancer service tag). The default NSG rule 65001 allows it unless a higher-priority deny blocks it.

cards.front: Data Path Availability vs Health Probe Status?
cards.back: Data Path: frontend reachability through to a healthy backend. Health Probe Status: each backend's own probe results.

cards.front: Backend VM to its own internal load balancer frontend?
cards.back: Not supported; that flow fails.

cards.front: Platform metrics: collection and retention?
cards.back: Automatic, every minute; kept 93 days; one chart shows up to 30 days.

cards.front: What's collected automatically vs configured?
cards.back: Automatic: platform metrics, activity log. Configure: resource logs (diagnostic setting), guest data (Azure Monitor Agent + DCR).

cards.front: Diagnostic setting destinations?
cards.back: Log Analytics workspace, storage account, event hub, partner solution.

cards.front: Workspace retention limits?
cards.back: Default 30 days (31 in price); analytics up to 2 years; total up to 12 years (long-term, read via search jobs).

cards.front: Log Analytics agent status?
cards.back: Retired August 2024. Use the Azure Monitor Agent with data collection rules.

cards.front: KQL: filter, choose columns, add column, aggregate?
cards.back: where, project, extend, summarize ... by (with bin() for time).

cards.front: Alert on resource deletion?
cards.back: Activity log alert rule.

cards.front: Alert on a KQL result?
cards.back: Log search alert rule (runs the query on a schedule).

cards.front: What's an action group?
cards.back: Reusable notifications (email, SMS, push, voice) and actions (runbook, Function, Logic App, webhook, ITSM, Event Hubs).

cards.front: What does an alert processing rule do?
cards.back: Acts on fired alerts in a scope: suppress all action groups, or add action groups; always, one-time or recurring.

cards.front: Stateful vs stateless alert?
cards.back: Stateful (auto-resolve) resolves when the condition clears; stateless fires every time it's met.

cards.front: VM insights: agent, DCR, table?
cards.back: Azure Monitor Agent; DCR prefixed MSVMI-; InsightsMetrics. Map + Dependency agent retire June 30, 2028.

cards.front: Network Watcher enablement?
cards.back: Automatic per region when you create a VNet; free; lives in NetworkWatcherRG.

cards.front: Connection monitor needs?
cards.back: Network Watcher agent extension on Azure VMs; Azure Arc + Azure Monitor Agent on-premises. Classic is deprecated.

cards.front: Recovery Services vault protects?
cards.back: Azure VMs, SQL/SAP HANA in VMs, Azure Files, on-premises (MARS, MABS, DPM). Also used by Site Recovery.

cards.front: Backup vault protects?
cards.back: Azure Disks, Azure Blobs, Azure Database for PostgreSQL (and more).

cards.front: Vault redundancy default and when it locks?
cards.back: Recovery Services vault defaults to GRS; locked once the first item is protected. Backup vault: set at creation.

cards.front: Cross Region Restore requirements?
cards.back: GRS vault; extra cost; up to 48 hours to activate; can't be reverted; vault-tier points only.

cards.front: Soft delete for backups?
cards.back: On by default; 14 extra days at no cost. Enhanced soft delete: custom retention, can be always-on (irreversible).

cards.front: Standard vs Enhanced VM policy?
cards.back: Standard: daily, snapshots 1-5 days. Enhanced: every 4-24 hours, snapshots 1-30 days, required for Premium SSD v2 and Ultra; can't go back.

cards.front: VMs per backup policy?
cards.back: Up to 100.

cards.front: VM restore options?
cards.back: Create new VM, restore disks (+ template), replace existing (VM must exist), cross region (vault tier), file recovery.

cards.front: Why can't the vault be deleted?
cards.back: It still holds backup data, including soft-deleted items. Disable soft delete before deleting backup data.

cards.front: What does Site Recovery deploy when replication starts?
cards.back: Mobility service extension on the VM; cache storage account in the source region; replica disks in the target.

cards.front: Site Recovery default replication policy?
cards.back: Crash-consistent points every 5 minutes (fixed); 1-day retention; app-consistent snapshots off.

cards.front: Test failover vs failover?
cards.back: Test: isolated network, no impact on replication or production; clean up after. Failover: real; then commit and reprotect.

cards.front: After failover, are VMs protected?
cards.back: No. Reprotect them (replicate back), then fail back when ready.

cards.front: Built-in backup alerts?
cards.back: Security (Sev 0; can't be turned off) and job failures (Sev 1; on by default). Notify via alert processing rule + action group.

cards.front: Backup reports need?
cards.back: Vault diagnostic settings sending backup events to Log Analytics in resource-specific mode.
